diagram_math_checks.result: K1 vertices (0,0),(1,0),(1,1) give y<=x; K2 vertices (0,0),(0,1),(1,1) give x<=y. Label positions (0.72,0.35) and (0.28,0.65) lie strictly on those respective sides. The rendered square has all four outer segments and the red segment (0,0) to (1,1). The coordinate-based --cycle closes correctly; no added closure is needed.

The local-face-unisolvence supplier proves that affine edge means equal midpoint values. On the diagonal midpoint (1/2,1/2), both v1=1-2x+2y and v2=1+2x-2y equal 1. On bottom/right midpoints (1/2,0),(1,1/2), v1=0; on left/top midpoints (0,1/2),(1/2,1), v2=0. Thus the four corner dots denote geometric vertices, not CR degrees of freedom; F denotes the only interior edge. This agrees with local/global space and global-face-basis suppliers.

diagram_math_checks.check: Broken gradient and homogeneous mean boundary condition
diagram_math_checks.result: Verification 1.1 gives gradients (-2,2) and (2,-2), each with squared length 8. Two area-1/2 triangles yield squared L2 broken-gradient norm 8 and norm 2 sqrt(2). The bottom trace 1-2x has integral zero but is not identically zero. No pointwise boundary condition or continuity claim is added by the figure.
The full two-step Verification derives the polynomials, gradients, norm and edge-mean conditions algebraically from F1/F2, without invoking the diagram.
